summary: Single deployable monolith: React Native (Expo), Python + Django, PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) database on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. It keeps data in US regions, matches the team's languages and is estimated at $510-$950 per month.

architecture.name: monolith
architecture.justification: One deployable is the fastest to build and simplest to run for a team of 6 and 2 feature areas (realtime, file storage).

alternatives.why_not: Adds service boundaries, network calls and per-service deployment that this team does not need at this scale (team 6).
With 2 feature areas the code base stays small enough that formal module boundaries mostly add ceremony; adopt them once a third feature area arrives.
Per-request functions suit light, spiky work; this backend runs as a long-lived service on AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which suits websockets, background jobs and steady traffic better.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) matches the team's typescript skills; covers web and ios and android from one codebase; depends on native module quality.

alternatives.why_not: Flutter scores 2.3 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (2.3 points).

tradeoffs: Native modules outside the Expo SDK need a custom development build

backend.justification: Python + Django matches the team's python skills; CSRF, XSS, SQLi protections and auth on by default; is a proven choice for healthtech projects.

alternatives.why_not: Node.js + NestJS scores 0.8 points lower overall, mainly on time to market (1.0 points) and vendor lock-in (0.6 points).
Python + FastAPI scores 1.4 points lower overall, mainly on time to market (0.6 points) and vendor lock-in (0.6 points).

tradeoffs: Sync-first, so realtime needs Channels

database.choice: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL in N. Virginia (us-east-1)
database.justification: PostgreSQL can be placed in N. Virginia (us-east-1) to keep data in the US; carries HIPAA attestation; has headroom for the expected load; row-level security, mature auditing, encryption. It runs as Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, the managed service on the same cloud as the application, so backups, patching and failover are the provider's job.

alternatives.why_not: Supabase Postgres scores 1.5 points lower overall, mainly on compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.5 points) and maintainability (0.4 points).
Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL scores 1.6 points lower overall, mainly on vendor lock-in (0.9 points) and cost (0.8 points).

tradeoffs: Write scaling beyond one primary needs design

hosting.justification: AWS Elastic Beanstalk runs on AWS as preferred; can be placed in N. Virginia (us-east-1) to keep data in the US; offers a 99.99% SLA, in line with the 99.9% target; VPC, IAM.

alternatives.why_not: AWS ECS on Fargate scores 0.1 points lower overall, mainly on vendor lock-in (0.6 points).
AWS EC2 (self-managed VMs) scores 0.6 points lower overall, mainly on time to market (0.6 points).

tradeoffs: Less active than ECS/Amplify

alternatives.why_not: A separate auth service (about $19-$42 per month, one more system to run) when Framework built-in auth (sessions/JWT) already covers this inside the core stack; worth it once the built-in option hits its limits. Score 0.74 vs 0.84.

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 90 requests/second and about 19M requests/month from 40K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.9% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.

warnings.message: HIPAA needs a signed business associate agreement with the host, database and every vendor that touches health data.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
No cache layer: about 90 requests/second and 40,000 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.
